name: Al-Masʿūdī completes Murūj al-Dhahab
summary: After three decades of travel from the Caspian to the Indus and down the East African coast, the polymath ʿAlī al-Masʿūdī completes Murūj al-Dhahab wa-Maʿādin al-Jawhar ('The Meadows of Gold and Mines of Gems'), an encyclopedic universal history and geography in 30 books.

_quarry.structural_significance: The most ambitious surviving 10th-century Arabic geographical-historical synthesis; foundational text of the maximal-curiosity Adab tradition of medieval Arabic encyclopedism. His emphasis on non-Muslim peoples (Hindus, Zoroastrians, Slavs) makes him an early comparative ethnographer.
